lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Kell, 2031. Six timber buildings on a shelf of rock, a well that works, and the smell of cut pine everywhere. Nothing is bricked up, because nothing has happened yet.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: This is the founding year of my order. I have read our charter every winter of my life — the whole thing, aloud, it takes an hour — and I have never once seen the hand that wrote it.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: It is being written this week. By somebody who is still deciding what to put in it.

lines.speaker: dax
lines.text: Smells like a building site. Everything worth being frightened of is still in a lab somewhere, and nobody's afraid of a lab yet.

lines.speaker: ilse
lines.text: You came up the mountain without a cart and you're not dressed for it, which means you either got lost or you came on purpose, and nobody gets lost this high.

lines.speaker: ilse
lines.text: Ilse Kell. I dug that well. That's the whole of my authority here and I find it holds up, so: what do you want.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: There is already a second party on the terrace: a woman in a very good coat with a leather case at her feet, and two small flying machines holding station above her shoulder.

lines.speaker: vance
lines.text: Aurelia Vance, counsel to Meridian. I was here first, and I am also waiting for an answer, so I suggest we take it in the order we arrived.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Auditor. Whatever is settled on this terrace this week, my order inherits. So does the village below it. So does the fortress it becomes in 2148, and the free town it is in 2312.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Three hundred years of people, standing on a decision about a well.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Speak to Ilse Kell, or to Vance, when you are ready to weigh in.
